name: Mount Everest
baseNote: South Base Camp (Nepal side), 5,364 m. The Tibetan side starts a little lower (North Base Camp, about 5,150 m); from the Tibetan Plateau Everest is usually quoted as rising about 3.7 km. Base-camp heights are not verified here.
fact: The highest point above sea level: 8,848.86 m by the 2020 Nepal-China survey. Its base is already on a plateau more than 5 km up.
widthNote: Half-width 8.8 km: the straight-line distance from Base Camp to the summit, about 8.8 km, as reported by trekking sources. Approximate and not verified against a survey; the profile is mirrored to the other side.

name: Mauna Kea
summitNote: Sources give 4,205 to 4,207 m (13,796 to 13,803 ft).
baseNote: Base on the ocean floor: NOAA and Guinness give about 10,205 to 10,210 m from base to summit; where the base begins is debated.
fact: Only 4.2 km of it is above the waves. From its base on the Pacific floor it rises about 10.2 km, more than Everest does above sea level.
widthNote: Half-width 60 km: assumed to be like its neighbour Mauna Loa, whose base is about 120 km across (NASA Goddard). A figure for Mauna Kea itself was not found, so this is an estimate.
